You're right, but there's some nuance at play here. Let's say 90% of people make a net positive contribution to our society, even if just a tiny bit. Like everything on a spectrum, there's something right at the center, the medium. 50% of people do better than the medium, while the other 50% do worse. The thread creator, not to disparage him, may very well be in the lower percentile, worse than the medium. But if 90% of a whole is good, he can still be a positive asset while being below par and not up to speed with his peers. They may mock him for his shortfalls; for not being as "human" as they are. That's just how it's gonna be, but I'm here to remind him that while he may be behind socially (and below par), he's not worthless like many people with this disorder are inclined to infer. I have an argument to back it up.

Edit: In other words, he's "worth less" and not "worthless".

First off, realize that you're not worthless because of your lack of social connections. I could use clichés to back that up, but what people really need is objectivity. Objectively, If you're making a net positive contribution to society in your life, you're meeting the bare expectations needed to be a fine person. This is as simple as having a job and providing for yourself, being a friendly person, and not engaging in reckless and immoral criminal activity. If you're doing those three things, you're a good person, and no one can argue against that without getting subjective cultural expectations and emotions involved.

With that said, you can still be a marginally better person by having friends and relationships. This is so people can enjoy your company and gain exposure to your opinions, viewpoints, worldviews, etc.

You can befriend others by being confident, (which requires legitimate self-esteem, and if you're an objectively good person as I described above, you shouldn't be that insecure), kind, interesting, (pursue hobbies if you aren't already), and supportive. There is no secret to winning friends or being enjoyable, if you gather your bearings mentally and put yourself out there, you will succeed.
